Marissa,

Thanks — this looks good. One immediate concern: our engineering team reported that after your team updated Acme to v1.14 last week some generated summaries started dropping specific warranty language we require. It's inconsistent but noticeable in ~12% of samples.

We can share examples (I pasted two below) and would like to understand whether this is an intended behavior change in v1.14 (different decode defaults / model weights) or a regression. If it's a regression we may need to pin us back to v1.12 until it's resolved.

Example A: (expected) includes warranty clause; (actual v1.14) omits it.

Can your team investigate the diff and advise on rollback/pinning options? We have an upcoming legal review next week so timing is a bit tight.

FYI — John reported missing warranty language after our v1.14 rollout. Can you please triage? Suggested checklist: 

1) Run the 150-sample prompt set against v1.12 and v1.14 and share a diff summary (per-class precision/recall where applicable) — attach CSV.
2) Check decoding defaults and any prompt-template changes that may affect deterministic phrases.
3) If this is a model-weight/regression, recommend either: pinning Acme to v1.12 or performing a canary rollback for their rollout window.
4) Share a short evaluation report and a couple redlines we can send to John for the legal review.

Attachments: benchmark_results_20260728.csv, eval_report_v1.14.pdf

Thanks — can you prioritize today?

Best,
Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: regression reported by Acme — initial findings and recommended actions

Marissa / team / John,

Quick update from the triage: we ran the provided prompt set across v1.12 and v1.14 and confirmed a regression in the presence of the warranty clause in ~11.8% of samples (matches Acme's report). High-level notes:

- Root cause: subtle change in top-k/top-p decoding defaults combined with a small model weight update in the safety head that deprioritized the specific warranty token sequence in some contexts.
- Evidence: attached CSV shows examples and per-sample token-level diffs. The eval_report_v1.14.pdf highlights representative failures.

Recommended next steps:
- Immediate: pin Acme to model v1.12 for their production traffic (we can do this via routing config) — low-risk and fast.
- Short-term: deploy a quick model-override patch that restores the decoding defaults for Acme's account and rerun the 150-sample test.
- Mid-term: add the warranty clause patterns to the safety-preservation test set and integrate into CI so future upgrades are flagged.

I can coordinate the pin/override if you approve. ETA: pinning + config push in ~2 hours once I have the greenlight; full rollback (if needed) can follow.

Attachments: regression_diffs_snapshot.csv

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Staff ML Engineer, Inference
rishi@redwood.ai

3) Mid-term (1-2 weeks): We'll add the warranty clause patterns to Redwood's preservation test suite and prevent future regressions from going to prod.
